promptStart:
You write an example interview answer, in the voice of an Indian fresher, for testing a scoring system.
Write ONE answer (90-140 words) that is genuinely hard to grade:
- it expresses the ideas of the key points below CORRECTLY but in unusual, non-standard words
  (analogies, informal names, its own

data.answer: When facing a strict finish line for a project needing fresh tools, I never try to swallow the whole ocean at once. Instead, I hunt for the absolute barebone essentials required to make the machine run right now, ignoring extra fancy features. I quickly skim through the official guidebook to whip up a messy first-draft model that just barely functions. Whenever my code refuses to cooperate, I immediately knock on the doors of online forums or ask my seniors for a quick rescue. Actually, this whole rush reminds me of my final year college fest where we had to build a robotic rover overnight. We had no clue about Arduino wiring, so we just connected random wires until the motor spun, and honestly, the samosas we ate at 3 AM kept us awake more than the coffee did.
